operator_io_quirks: DDL uses backtick-quoted identifiers (`aircraft`, `aid`) and double-quoted FK columns; sqlite_master stores them verbatim — writer must replay DDL as-is, not re-quote.
Declared types are Oracle-style: number(4,0), number(7,2), varchar2(20), date. 'varchar2' is NOT in the char family list (char,text,blob) so it falls to the crash fallback -> String; record.

departure_date/arrival_date declared 'date' but storage class is TEXT with format 'MM/DD/YYYY HH:MM' (e.g. '04/12/2005 09:30'). First element does not parse as int, so Date fuzzer; none of the 7 upstream templates match this format -> template detection fails, falls to default range.
price has mixed storage classes (real and integer) in same column; salary/distance stored as integer despite number(10,2)/number(6,0) declared.
All columns notnull=0 (no NOT NULL constraints) and no CHECK constraints; PKs are the only enforced constraints.
certificate has composite PK (eid,aid) and two FKs to employee/aircraft; both parents exist and are unique on their PKs.
flight.aid FK -> aircraft.aid; aircraft has 16 rows, flight 10 rows, so FK values are a subset — TS will draw with replacement from parent's final values.
Tiny tables (10-69 rows): original_values sampling (k=min(5,len)) will use nearly all distinct values; literal pool from train SQL will dominate.
Table names all lowercase, no spaces; column names lowercase; no mixed-case issues here.
Self-references: none. Cycles: none (flight->aircraft, certificate->employee, certificate->aircraft).
employee.name has 30 distinct over 31 rows (one duplicate) — not declared unique, so drop_unique_duplicates won't touch it.
flight.origin has only 2 distinct values ('Los Angeles','Chicago') — heavy skew; TS String fuzzer will produce many fresh random strings, losing this skew.
operator_ts_expectations: flno/aid/eid: Number fuzzer with scale=0 (number(4,0) etc.), range [-10^0,10^0]=[-1,1] for flno (scale 0) — wait, scale from (a,b): a=4,b=0 -> scale=4, precision=0; range [-10^4,10^4]. Fresh ints perturbed by +-1/+-2.
eid number(9,0): range [-10^9,10^9]; original eids are 8-9 digit ints, so fresh draws plausible but perturbed values may collide with PK -> dropped.
price number(7,2): scale=7, range [-10^7,10^7] floats; original prices ~200-300, so fresh draws are wildly implausible (FN driver: price comparisons in gold SQL will rarely match).
distance number(6,0): range [-10^6,10^6]; original 1500-8400, fresh draws plausible-ish but wide.

departure_date/arrival_date: Date fuzzer, no template matches 'MM/DD/YYYY HH:MM' -> default 1800-2100 range, formatted by first parsable template (likely none -> fallback). Text-stored dates will be replaced by random datetimes in a different format -> gold SQL date comparisons (e.g. departure_date > '...') will mostly fail (FN).

origin/destination/name: String fuzzer, length range from original (origin max ~11, destination ~15, name ~30), fresh random strings over a-zA-Z0-9() — 'Los Angeles' style values lost; gold SQL with origin='Los Angeles' will match only via literal pool (p=0.2 element reuse).
aircraft.name: String, original 'Boeing 747-400' etc.; fresh strings lose the 'Boeing'/'Airbus' prefix structure -> LIKE 'Boeing%' queries fail (FN).
certificate composite PK (eid,aid): sample_fresh_primary_keys drops duplicate (eid,aid) pairs; with 20*15 possible pairs and n~30-2000 rows, many duplicates dropped -> small certificate tables.

FK flight.aid drawn from aircraft.aid final values (16 distinct) with replacement -> flight rows may repeat aid, fine; but if aircraft PK filtering drops rows, flight.aid may reference missing aircraft (FK not enforced, pragma off).
employee.salary number(10,2): range [-10^10,10^10]; original 100k-256k; fresh draws implausible -> salary comparisons (e.g. salary > 100000) mostly fail (FN).

Known FP source: TS does not enforce NOT NULL, so NULLs can appear where original had none; but all columns nullable here so no constraint failures — instead type-affinity mismatches (text in number column) may cause sqlite to store as text, changing comparison semantics.
